full_judgment:
This revisional application arises out of the judgment and order dated 30-5-79 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1977 passed by the learned Munsif 1st Court, Sylhet in Miscellaneous Case No-76 of 1970 arising out of a an application for pre-emption under section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act. 1949. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of this Rule are that the petitioner instituted the said Miscellaneous Case under section 24 of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act stating that the land appertains to khatian No. 554 and it constituted a residential homestead with adjuncts not connected with agriculture. The petitioner is a co-sharer in the case land and the opposite party No. 1 is a stranger and no notice was served about the sale dated 5-11-69, as such, the petitioner is entitled to pre-empt the case land. The said pre-emption case was opposed by the opposite party No. 1 contending that petitione's case is not maintainable under section 24 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act inasmuch as the purchase made by two separate Kabalas and two separate cases ought to have been filed by the petitioner. On a review of the evidence led, the trial Court allowed the pre-emption case in favour of the petitioner against which the opposite party No. 1 preferred appeal and the lower appellate Court upon hearing the parties reversed the decision of the trial Court and allowed the appeal. The petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesiid decision of the lower appellate Court moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. It has been further submitted that the lower appellate Court misconstrued the provision of section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 as well as the provision of section 24 of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act 1949 and thereby misdirected himself in disallowing the petitioner's application for pre-emption causing failure of justice. 

 5. Mr. BK Das, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, contends that the suit holding comprised of two plots namely the plot No. 1975 as chara land and plot No. 1936 as a homestead land and because of two plots being included in the same Khatian No. 544 and situated in the rural area are agricultural homestead land and, as such, the right of pre-emption will accrue under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and not under Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and therefore the court of appeal below rightly held that the petitioner's application under section 24 of the East Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act was not maintainable. 

 6. Mr. Das has further argued that if it is accepted that the homestead plot is unconnected with agriculture then the right of pre-emption accrues under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and the other plot attached to the homested being as agricultural land then the pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act will arise and in that situation a question of partial pre-emption in respect of the lands of the same Khatian will arise and it is not permissible as a settled principle of law. 

 7. While repelling the above contention of Mr. BK Das, Mr. Matin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, having clborated his submission, argued that the word holding as defined in sub-section (13) of section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act means "a parcel or parcels of land or an undivided share thereof held by a raiyat or an under-raiyat and forming the subject of separate tenancy" and as such the word "Homestead" as defind in sub-section (14) of section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the word "non-agricultural land" as defined in sub-section (4) of section 2 of the Non agricultural Tenancy Act are both holding with regard to the nature and character of the holding. Mr. Matin thus contends that the suit holding being homestead with adjuncts is unconnected with agriculture held by a non-agricultural tenant is pre-emptible under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 9. The only point that has arisen in this revision is whether an application for pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act in respect of the homestead with adjunct lands not within municipal area is maintainable. 

 11. The word holding has been defined in sub-section (13) of section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which means a parcel or parcels of land or an undivided share thereof held by a raiyat or an under raiyat and forming the subject of separate tenancy. 

 13. The expression non-agricultural land has been defined in section 2(4) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act: 

 15. It appears that the suit holding being homestead with adjuncts is admittedly situated in the rural area. It is true that a homestead land cannot be a raiyati land (agricultural land) even if some part of the land is used for gardening or growing vegetables or for the purposes connected with agriculture but the fact remains the holding does not lose the character of homestead. In the instant case the determining factor is of the situation of homestead. Considering the nature and character of the suit holding and its situation. I am of the view that the homestead with adjunct is very much connected with agriculture. There is nothing on record to show the suit holding was used for the purposes not connected with agriculture and it is non agricultural land for all practical purposes. It is profitable to cite a case of Lutfun Nahar vs. Syeeda Hashmat Ara Begum reported in 21 DLR 633 to find a complete answer to the arguments advanced by Mr. Matin. Their Lordships held in the aforesaid decision that homestead within a municipality or non-agricultural land cannot be pre-empted under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of principle laid down in the said decision. I hold that the suit holding being homestead situated in the rural area is an agricultural land and section 96 of the Act is only available.
